records.name: Ucayali
records.summary:
The documented evidence binding a trans visitor in Ucayali is national in scope. In February 2025 the congressional Women and Family Commission unanimously approved bills 6506 and 8457 barring trans people from public restrooms corresponding to their gender rather than their birth sex, with narrow exceptions for custody, medical care and accompanying children under 12, the elderly or disabled, and a ban on ambiguous signage; the plenary approved the fused law on 2 April 2025 without a second vote, in a package a national human-rights institute frames as legalized discrimination against trans access to public space. A July 2023 complaint over gendered bathroom labels at the capital's airport set the process in motion; activists object that the measures weaponize stigma.

Ucayali has no recorded local ordinance, incident series or enforcement pattern, and official data carry no departmental breakdown — the national framework is the only documented determinant of conditions here.

records.name: Junín
records.summary: No region-specific trans law, ordinance, incident series or enforcement finding was located for this division - the research dossier lists it among the units with no sub-national signal, so the national evidence applies: the congressional Women and Family Committee approved bills banning trans people from public restrooms in early 2025 (floor vote pending), and the national university observatory recorded 54 LGBTI homicides and 170 rights violations in 2020-2023, more than half of the homicide victims trans women (30 of 54). The absence of local findings reflects Peru's lack of hate-crime statistics rather than any positive local difference.

records.name: Ica
records.summary:
Ica has no recorded trans-specific regional law, ordinance or enforcement pattern; the national framework applies unchanged. In February 2025 the congressional Women and Family Commission unanimously approved bills 6506 and 8457 barring trans people from public restrooms matching their gender rather than their birth sex, with narrow exceptions (custody, medical care, accompanying under-12s, elderly or disabled people) and a ban on ambiguous signage; the plenary approved the fused text on 2 April 2025 without a second vote, a package a national human-rights institute frames as legalized discrimination against trans access to public space.

Violence data is national: the Cayetano Heredia University TLGBI rights observatory recorded 54 LGBTI homicides and 170 rights violations in 2020-2023 — trans women the most affected (30 of 54), 19 killings in 2023 — with torture-level violence and a February 2023 gang extortion-murder of a trans sex worker in central Lima. Peru has no hate-crime law, so regional comparisons cannot come from official statistics; nothing marks Ica as different either way.

records.name: Cusco
records.summary: No documented sub-national signal for Cusco: the country dossier lists this department among the regions where no region-specific trans law, ordinance, incident series or enforcement finding could be located, and all three attached sources are national in scope. What binds Cusco is the national frame: a congressional bill package (6506/8457, committee-approved February 2025) would bar trans people from public sanitary facilities of the opposite sex at birth, and national data record 54 killings and 170 rights-violation cases of TLGBI people between 2020 and 2023 with trans women most affected and hate crimes rising - no regional deviation documented either way.
